mappings.note: Finds the rhyme partner of 'crow' in the first stanza. Rhyme is a formal literary convention, C-E1.4.
The shift from a rueful to a lifted mood is the speaker's inner change, LO-2.
Asks for the opening mood AND the images that create it - tone and imagery, both matters of craft that no LO in this frame names, so C-E1.4.
Both live parts read Lomov's soliloquy for what he actually feels and for the uncertainty in his tone - character analysis, LO-2.
Part i retrieves why the peasants came to treat the land as theirs (LO-1); part ii asks what the speech shows about Lomov's character (LO-2).
Part i retrieves Lomov's territorial claim (LO-1); the rest read Natalya's sudden shift of ground, which is character in context (LO-2).
Parts i and ii retrieve where the quarrel starts and what 'them' refers to (LO-1); part iii judges Natalya's temper (LO-2); part iv asks for a phrase meaning 'postpone' (C-E1.1).
Every part reads the soliloquy for what it reveals about Lomov's calculation and his nerves - character analysis, LO-2.

Asks what the two sides should have done instead - the learner's own recommendation, C-E1.2.
A character sketch of Lomov. LO-2 covers character analysis; no quoted evidence is demanded.
A character description of Natalya around named traits. LO-2.

'Elaborate with reference to the poem' requires the answer to be built on the text - evidence, LO-3.
